feeling: {H} looked at the endless stars and felt very small, and very happy to be there.

{H} wondered what {P} would look like up close, and hoped it would be friendly.
{H} missed home a little, especially the smell of toast, but kept going.
What if {I} was lost for good? {H} shook that thought away and kept going.
{H} decided that being curious was the best superpower in the whole galaxy.
Even with all those buttons, {H} felt a little nervous. That was all right, thought {H}.

It was a big universe, but {H} had a big plan, and that felt just right.
{H} remembered a bedtime story about the stars, and the memory felt warm and safe.
Was {V} really so bad? {H} wondered if everyone just wanted to be understood.
{H} promised to be kind, no matter how strange the creatures were.

{H} wanted to find {I} more than anything, and that wish kept {H} going.

setting: The air at {P} tasted recycled and faintly of metal, and a low hum ran beneath every other sound, steady as a pulse.
Screens glowed across {P}, each showing the same calm message. Nobody seemed to be reading them.
Nearby, {W}. The light at {P} had the flat, shadowless quality of something designed to be looked at, not lived in.
Beyond {P2}, a distant machine ticked through its slow cycle. {P} felt like the inside of a clock that had forgotten what it was counting.
Lights at {P} dimmed on a schedule no one had explained, and a faint chime marked each hour as though to remind everyone.
{P} was quieter than it ought to be. Even the ventilation seemed to be holding back, listening for something.
Cold light spilled across {P}, and {W}. Nobody looked up. Looking up was how you got noticed.
Static hissed on every channel around {P}, a soft grey noise that made the silence behind it seem enormous.
At {P}, the metal was cool and faintly vibrating underfoot, the way a machine feels when it is thinking.
An automated voice made an announcement at {P}, calm and pleasant, and completely at odds with the faces of those who heard it.
Dust drifted through the pale light at {P}, turning slowly, as though gravity there were merely a suggestion.
Every surface at {P} was clean in a way that suggested effort, and fear of what would happen if it were not.
The distant glow beyond {P} was either a sunrise or a fire. From here, {H} could not tell, and nobody had said.
A faint electric smell hung over {P}: ozone and warm plastic, the smell of too many machines working too hard.
action: {H} worked through the diagnostics line by line, thumb moving down the cracked screen, stopping only when the numbers stopped making sense.
Quietly, {H} slipped past {P2}, keeping to the edge of the light and timing each step to the rhythm of the sweeping scanners.
{A} unrolled a worn schematic and {H} traced the route with a finger: three corridors, two junctions, one door that should not have been there.
{H} knelt at the access panel, pried it open with a coin, and began untangling wires by feel, counting under their breath.
{A2} watched the exits while {H} copied the data to a small, battered drive, one anxious percentage point at a time.
{H} climbed the service ladder near {P2}, rung by rung, resisting the urge to look down at how far the floor had gone.
Moving in short, deliberate bursts, {H} crossed {P} between sweeps of the scanner, then pressed flat against the wall to wait.
{H} recalibrated the receiver, turning the dial a hair's width at a time until the static thinned into something like a voice.
{A} pulled a hood low, and {H} did the same. They walked towards {P2} at the exact pace of everyone else, which was the whole trick.
{H} scanned the readout, frowned, and made a note on the back of one hand, because anything written down could be found.
{A2} hacked the door lock while {H} counted the seconds aloud, very softly, until the little light turned from red to green.
{H} unpacked the kit on the floor: a torch, a coil of cable, a battered handheld, and a promise made to somebody who was no longer there.
With one eye on the clock, {H} rerouted the power cables near {P2}, and the corridor lights stuttered and held.
{H} memorised the patrol pattern around {P}: four minutes out, ninety seconds of silence, and the sweep returning like a tide.
talk: "The signal is still strong," said {A}, eyes on the screen. "That's impossible," said {H}. "Nothing out there should be transmitting."
"Tell me you didn't touch it," said {H}. {A2} said nothing, which was an answer.
"How long do we have?" asked {H}. {A} glanced at the display. "Less than I'd like. More than I fear."
"They'll know we were here," said {A2}. "Good," said {H}. "Let them wonder what we wanted."
"What if we {T}?" said {H} slowly. {A} stared. "That's either genius or the worst idea you've had." "It might be both."
"You don't have to come," said {H}. {A} snorted. "I stopped believing in the safe option a long time ago."
"Does {V} know?" whispered {A2}. "Everyone knows something," said {H}. "The question is what they'll do with it."
"Keep your voice down," breathed {A}. "These walls listen." {H} nodded once and mouthed the rest.
"The data's corrupted," said {A2}, turning the screen. {H} leant closer. "No. It's been edited. Look at the timestamps."
"I keep thinking about {I}," said {H}. "Why would anyone hide something so carefully, unless it could change everything?"
"Say the word," said {A}, hand on the switch. {H} looked towards {P2}, breathed in, and said it.
"Tell me honestly," said {H}. "Is this still the plan, or are we making it up as we go?" {A} grinned. "Yes."
"I used to think the system was broken," said {A2}. "Now I think it works exactly as intended."

feeling: {H} thought about everyone who would never know what had been decided on their behalf, and felt the weight of it settle like cold metal.
It would be easy to believe the calm voices. {H} had believed them once, for years, and remembered how comfortable it was.
Fear was a quiet thing in a place like this. It lived in the shoulders, in the held breath, in the habit of not looking back.
{H} wondered whether anybody had ever stood in this exact spot and chosen differently. If so, the records did not say.
{H} remembered the sound of an old song, a real one, sung out of tune, and held on to it as proof that other worlds had existed.
Doubt arrived, quiet and reasonable: what if {V} had a point, and the rules existed for a reason? {H} turned the thought over, and set it down.
{H} was tired in a way that sleep could not fix, but {I} was out there, and that made tiredness feel like a luxury.
Stars or streetlights, it made no difference: {H} had always looked up and wished for a door somewhere. Tonight, there might be one.
{H} knew the odds. Everyone did. They were printed on the walls to discourage hope, and hope, stubbornly, had not read them.
For the first time in a long while, {H} felt like the author of the next minute rather than its passenger.
{H} thought of {A} and felt a strange, steadying loyalty. It was not something the systems had accounted for.
What was left of home, {H} wondered, once the maps were redrawn and the names were changed? Perhaps only the habit of looking for it.
{H} could turn back. The thought was clean and tempting, like cool water, and {H} drank it in and kept walking.
There was no heroic music, {H} noted, only the hum of machinery and the sound of a pulse. It would have to be enough.
